display.purpose: High-contrast editorial serif, large & sparing: greetings, marquee headings, the 'All clear.' state. Display-only.

body.purpose: The grotesk workhorse: all UI text, table cells, form values.

label.purpose: Technical mono with tabular figures: metrics, counts, timestamps, uppercase tracked micro-labels. Never running prose.

shadows.name: whisper-lift
shadows.purpose: Soft, low depth (theme-aware via Ant boxShadowTertiary) on data-bearing panels only — the Home readout and queue cards. A whisper, not a drop shadow; in dark it yields to the hairline border.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Ant Design's heavier default on genuinely floating overlays (dropdowns, popovers, modals, notifications).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Standard transition duration for interactive state changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default confirming action — monochrome ink fill, never red.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #141416; color: #ffffff; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; padding: 4px 15px; height: 32px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.645,0.045,0.355,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2a2a2e; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #141416; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #0d0d0e; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive or irreversible actions only — the rare place red fills a control.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { background: #d92d2d; color: #ffffff; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; padding: 4px 15px; height: 32px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.645,0.045,0.355,1); } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #e35a5a; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #d92d2d; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Default Button
components.css: .ds-btn-default { background: transparent; color: #141416; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; padding: 4px 15px; height: 32px; border: 1px solid rgba(5,5,5,0.15); border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-default:hover { color: #d92d2d; border-color: #d92d2d; } .ds-btn-default:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #141416; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nav Item (selected)
components.description: The selected rail item — a Signal Red block with white text on the dark rail. The single most prominent use of red.
components.css: .ds-rail { background: #0c0c0d; padding: 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; width: 200px; } .ds-nav-item { display: block; padding: 8px 12px; border-radius: 6px; color: rgba(245,242,234,0.72); font-size: 14px; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s, background 0.2s; } .ds-nav-item:hover { color: #f5f2ea; background: rgba(245,242,234,0.06); } .ds-nav-item--selected { background: #d92d2d; color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Flat surface separated by a hairline border — no shadow at rest.
components.html:
Team A
6 members · 3 open tasks
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; color: #141416; border: 1px solid rgba(5,5,5,0.1); border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card__title { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-card__body { font-size: 12px; color: rgba(20,20,22,0.55); }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: The standard filter control — hairline border, leading magnifier, no colored focus glow.
components.css: .ds-search { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid rgba(5,5,5,0.15); border-radius: 6px; padding: 4px 11px; height: 32px; color: rgba(20,20,22,0.45); transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-search:focus-within { border-color: #141416; color: #141416; } .ds-search input { border: none; outline: none; background: transparent; font-size: 14px; color: #141416; width: 240px; }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: Small squared status pill — access levels and states. Neutral by default; red only for danger/overdue.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; line-height: 20px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: rgba(5,5,5,0.04); color: #141416; border: 1px solid rgba(5,5,5,0.12); } .ds-tag--danger { background: rgba(217,45,45,0.08); color: #d92d2d; border-color: rgba(217,45,45,0.3); }

components.name: Segmented Toggle
components.description: Mutually-exclusive view switch (e.g. Calendar General/Me, rows-per-page) — bordered track, sliding thumb, monochrome.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; background: rgba(5,5,5,0.05); border-radius: 6px; padding: 2px; gap: 2px; } .ds-seg__item { border: none; background: transparent; font-size: 14px; color: rgba(20,20,22,0.65); padding: 3px 12px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-seg__item--active { background: #ffffff; color: #141416; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); } .ds-seg__item:hover:not(.ds-seg__item--active) { color: #141416; }

narrative.overview: This is the calm command surface a student robotics team runs its whole operation from — tasks, inventory, events, people, and the org itself, all readable at a glance. It is built on Ant Design v5, but its identity is a deliberate restraint layered on top: an almost entirely black-and-white world, precise and dense, where a single signal red appears only when something is active or needs attention. Nothing decorates; everything informs. The feeling is a well-lit console at rest — quiet until a light turns on. The system is Operate-first: scanability, consistency, and native form-control behavior outrank expression, and the brand lives in precise details rather than flourish. It ships light and dark as equal citizens — the left navigation rail stays dark in both themes, an anchoring constant like the bezel around a screen — and both are held to full contrast legibility.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome-dominant: black/white/ink/cream carry ~90% of every screen.
One reserved red for state and danger only.
Three self-hosted voices: editorial serif display, grotesk UI, technical-mono readout.
Flat base, with a soft whisper-lift on data-bearing panels.
Dual-theme by default; the dark rail is a fixed anchor.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Signal Red covers ≤10% of any screen and only ever means active or danger. If red is doing decoration, brand color, or a primary CTA fill, it is wrong. Its rarity is the entire point — when a light turns red, it matters.

rules.name: The No-Role-Color Rule
rules.body: Never color-code by job title or org rank. Authority in this product is data (seats + the access ladder), not a fixed identity, so color must not imply a hierarchy the system doesn't hardcode.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Numbers, counts, timestamps, and uppercase micro-labels are set in Geist Mono with tabular figures — the data reads like an instrument. Running prose and headings never use the mono; the mono never sets a paragraph.

rules.name: The One Serif Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif appears once or twice per surface, at large size, for a human beat (a greeting, a state). It is display-only — never a body, label, or control face. Its scarcity is what makes it feel considered.

rules.name: The Whisper-Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is soft and purposeful: only data-bearing panels lift, and only just enough to read as a surface. If a shadow announces itself, it's too strong. Hairline borders still do most of the separating.

dos: Do keep Signal Red (#d92d2d) for active/selected state and danger only — ≤10% of any screen (The One Red Rule).
Do use the three voices in their lanes: serif for large display beats, grotesk for UI/body, mono for metrics/labels/timestamps.
Do set counts, timestamps, and tabular data in Geist Mono with tabular figures (The Readout Rule).
Do treat light and dark as equal first-class themes, and keep the navigation rail dark in both.
Do give data-bearing panels a soft whisper-lift; separate everything else with hairline borders.
Do keep data dense and scannable, and use logical properties (marginInlineStart) for future RTL/Arabic.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue or use red as a primary-button fill or brand wash — the world is monochrome + one red.
Don't set the serif below display size, or use the mono for running prose — each voice stays in its lane.
Don't let a shadow announce itself; depth is a whisper on data surfaces, never a heavy drop shadow on at-rest cards.
Don't color-code roles, titles, or org rank — authority is data, not a fixed identity (The No-Role-Color Rule).
Don't hardcode pageSize on tables; use defaultPageSize so the size changer works.
